A4904710.name: ALMOND
bullets: Big 84 pound sweetheart who knows Sit and takes treats gently
Loves petting all over, greets people with a relaxed, wiggly body
Was gentle and tolerant at the vet even with a sore mouth, offering sits with no command
Leaned into potential adopters at a meet and greet and gave gentle kisses
Healing well from a tooth repair, almost done with his recovery
A4904710.story: Other dogs in the kennel wing wind him up, and it is hiding the mushy, people-loving boy the staff see the moment he is with humans. Get him away from the barking and he melts.
A4904710.needs: An experienced handler, an only-dog home for now, and no dog parks. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5168289.name: AUGGIE
bullets: Walks well on leash and will stay right by your side
Knows Sit and takes treats gently
Played tag with his handler in the yard and came in for pets and kisses
Ignored other dogs on walks, friendly and easy to handle
High energy outside, chill once he settles
A5168289.story: Outside his kennel he is a friendly, kissy, playful guy. Inside it, the noise and confinement are breaking him down fast, and he is running out of time to show anyone who he really is.
A5168289.needs: A calm home with real decompression time, slow introductions, and older kids only.

A5169459.name: BASS
bullets: Tiny 18 pound baby with a soft, wiggly body
Loves all petting and handling, wags his tail when you approach
Healing from a pelvis injury and getting a little stronger every day
A5169459.story: He is a three month old puppy with a broken pelvis, resting in a shelter kennel instead of a soft bed. With crate rest and vet care he has every chance at a full, zoomy puppy life.
A5169459.needs: Rescue placement with vet care for his healing pelvis. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5168810.name: BILLY
bullets: Gentle, shy boy who takes treats softly from your hand
Rests his head in your lap once he trusts you, and climbed right into a handler's lap
Runs to his person for comfort when something startles him
Chased a tennis ball and greeted a passing handler at the fence
Just 38 pounds, a small, lean Dobie
A5168810.story: Billy is scared of the world right now, but watch what happens when he decides you are safe: head in your lap, leaning in, checking in with you across the yard. He is a velcro dog waiting for a person.
A5168810.needs: A patient, quiet foster who will let him decompress and build trust at his own speed. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169280.name: COBALT
bullets: Gentle even when frightened, took food right from his finder's hand
Allowed all gentle petting and handling at his exam
Deeply bonded to the dog he was rescued with, they eat together and sleep close
No aggression ever noted, just a quiet, overwhelmed boy
A5169280.story: He survived a month on the streets and now he is shut down and sick, fighting a tick-borne illness and early heartworm. He needs someone to fight for him the way his dog friend never stopped sticking by him.
A5169280.needs: A rescue with vet support for tick-borne illness and heartworm treatment. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5149654.name: COCO
bullets: LOVES water: the pool, the hose, the sprinkler, all of it
Plays fetch and will trade you the ball for a treat
Knows Sit, Stay, Shake, Paw, and High Five
Crawls into your lap for belly rubs and leans in for affection
Volunteers call her sweet, sassy, and fun-loving
A5149654.story: Volunteers have adored this girl for months. She is a splashy, fetch-obsessed love who just needs the right home setup, and she is out of chances to wait for it.
A5149654.needs: An adult-only home, only dog for now, and mealtimes managed in her own space. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5168196.name: COLBY
bullets: Goofy, playful Golden with big puppy energy
Greets people with a loose body and a softly wagging tail
Walks on leash and loved exploring the yard with his handlers
Was friendly and playful with the female dogs in his last home
A5168196.story: He is a young Golden who never got the training or structure he needed, and he uses his mouth too much when he is excited or unsure. In the yard he is all wiggles, leaning in for neck scratches.
A5168196.needs: An experienced, adult-only handler who will go slow with touch and handling, no male dogs. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5168886.name: DENVER
bullets: Pocket-sized boy, under 10 pounds
His finder says he was friendly and playful with their 10 year old, approaching for attention
Playful with his little dog buddy Usher, they were found together
Calm energy with fun bursts of zoomies, per the family who found him
A5168886.story: The shelter has this little guy terrified and defending himself the only way a 9 pound dog knows how. Five days in a quiet home had him playing with a child. He needs that home back.
A5168886.needs: A patient, small-dog-savvy foster and a quiet space to decompress, no pressure. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5168853.name: HOPPER
bullets: Loves to play and is crazy about balls
His finder says he is great with cats, lets them sniff and play and never chases
Appears leash trained and rode calmly in the car
Greets people with a wiggly body and jumps for joy, literally
A5168853.story: Hopper is a big, bouncy young boy who loves people so hard he forgets his manners and jumps all over you. He is also fighting a cold and skipping meals, the shelter is wearing him down.
A5168853.needs: An experienced handler who can channel his energy and teach polite greetings. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5168989.name: MOMO
bullets: Slept curled up with the toddlers in his old home, gentle with kids as young as 2
House-trained and crate trained, knows "Bed" and basic commands
Mellow, friendly, and attention-seeking once he feels safe
Just 24 pounds of soft, sweet Aussie
A5168989.story: His family lost their housing and Momo lost everything he knew. In a home he was the gentle dog who slept with the children. In the shelter he is frozen with fear, and he cannot survive there.
A5168989.needs: A quiet, patient foster and real decompression time to become himself again. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169119.name: POMEGRANATE
bullets: Soft, wiggly 16 pound boy who solicits pets through the kennel door
Walks easily on leash with a soft, neutral body the whole way
Comes when called and accepts petting all over
Startles at first touch sometimes but settles fast and leans back in
A5169119.story: He is one year old, wiggly, and easy, the kind of dog who trots to the fence just to see what you are doing. A stray-life scuffle with another dog put him on this list, and people who handle him adore him.
A5169119.needs: A foster with no other pets for now and slow, careful dog introductions later. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5162499.name: SAKE
bullets: Jumps in and out of the pool like it is his job
Plays fetch with multiple toys in rotation and does full zoomies
Knows Sit and climbs into your lap like a 51 pound puppy
Leans in, licks your arm, and soaks up petting all over
A previous home says he was gentle with kids and licked their faces
A5162499.story: Sake is a lap dog in a heeler body, all pool splashes and face kisses. The kennel makes him frantic and grabby with the leash, and that frustration is being mistaken for who he is.
A5162499.needs: An experienced handler, decompression time, slow dog intros, and patience with some indoor marking at first. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5168530.name: SPOCK
bullets: Striking 79 pound black Shepherd
Walks on leash and tolerates petting on his head and back
Came outside when called this week, sniffed a hand, and gave gentle tail wags
Was found surviving on the streets with another dog
A5168530.story: Spock is shut down, skipping meals, and disappearing inside himself in that kennel. But this week he walked up, sniffed a hand, and wagged. He is still in there, asking someone to come get him.
A5168530.needs: An experienced, Shepherd-savvy handler and a quiet home with zero pressure while he decompresses. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5168885.name: USHER
bullets: Tiny 11 pound gentleman, found with his buddy Denver
His finder says he was friendly and playful with their 10 year old
Would approach the family for attention once he warmed up
Calm energy with playful bursts, per the home that found him
A5168885.story: In a home, this little guy warmed up in days and played with a child. In the shelter, he is trembling under chairs. Every hour in that kennel takes him further from the dog his finders knew.
A5168885.needs: A patient, small-dog-experienced foster and a quiet room to decompress in. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169138.name: ARIES
bullets: Lived with four boys ages 1 to 12, described as friendly and full of happy energy
Knows Sit and Come, and runs to the door when you grab the leash
Loves lounging in the kiddie pool
House-trained and friendly and playful with other dogs
Softened with his handler in the yard, leaning against their legs for pets
A5169138.story: Aries is a two year old Lab who never got training, and new people scare him until he decides you are okay. Then he sits against your legs and melts. His old family said it best: he needs someone with structure who will work with him.
A5169138.needs: An experienced handler, a secure 6 foot fence, and slow introductions to new people. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A4849043.name: CALLIE
bullets: Fetch fanatic who plays with multiple toys in rotation
Star of the shelter treadmill program, runs at a fast pace and loves it
Knows Sit and Stay and would do anything for a hot dog
Gives gentle kisses, leans in, and greets new people with a soft, wiggly body
Went on field trips and store outings and handled them like a champ
A4849043.story: Callie has waited since January. Volunteers have run with her, walked her, and loved her for seven months, and every note says the same thing: sweet, affectionate, happy girl. She guards her food and toys around other animals, so she needs to be the star of the show.
A4849043.needs: An experienced handler, an only-pet home, kids 12 and up, and no small animals.

A5167420.name: DELILAH
bullets: Barely more than a puppy, found in a river bottom with another dog
Crawled right into a volunteer's lap and let herself be carried to the yard
"Very sweet but shy girl" per the people who know her
The shelter terrifies her, she trembles and hides in her kennel
Ignores other dogs completely on walks
A5167420.story: She is not broken, she is scared. Every volunteer who slows down for her finds the same soft, gentle girl underneath.
A5167420.needs: A quiet, patient foster and real decompression time, no forcing, let her come to you. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5167643.name: DWIGHT
bullets: "Calm, mellow, easy going, gentle sweet boy" straight from his eval
Loves tennis balls and a slow game of fetch
Walks on a loose leash, ignores other dogs, takes treats nicely
Fighting a stubborn cold he cannot shake in the shelter, and he has stopped eating well
Tied to a chair in the lobby and abandoned, he never got a goodbye
A5167643.story: An 8 year old gentleman who plays slow fetch and just wants a couch to get better on. Seniors deserve soft landings.
A5167643.needs: A foster home where he can rest, finish his meds, and see a vet for his lingering cold. Go-slow family introductions recommended.

A5168967.name: EARL
bullets: Shy shepherd boy who is deeply frightened by the shelter
Takes treats from your hand once he decides you are safe
Walks on leash and ignores other dogs completely
Came in underweight and is now getting fed twice a day
Touch-shy, he needs people who let him set the pace
A5168967.story: He is not asking for much. Just quiet, groceries, and a person who does not reach for him before he is ready.
A5168967.needs: An experienced, patient handler and hands-off decompression time. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5167288.name: FANTASTIC
bullets: "Happy go lucky" and "such a GOOD boy" per multiple volunteers
Knows Sit, takes treats gently, appears potty trained
Does a leisurely jog around the yard, then comes back for face rubs
Walked right up to a stranger in the hallway to say hi
His left eye has gone droopy and he needs a vet to figure out why
A5167288.story: Seven years old, mellow, affectionate, and running out of time over one droopy eye. Seniors deserve soft landings.
A5167288.needs: A foster who can get his eye checked by a vet. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169074.name: GORDO
bullets: His owner passed away, that is the only reason he is here
His family called him "very friendly and loving" and playful and goofy
Lived with kids ages 4, 6, and 9
Knows Sit, Stay, and Lay Down, crate trained and leash trained
In the shelter he has completely shut down, scared and hard to read
A5169074.story: Everything Gordo knew disappeared overnight. The dog in that kennel is grief and fear, not who he is at home.
A5169074.needs: A patient foster and serious decompression time to grieve and land. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169156.name: JACKSON
bullets: Lived with kids ages 7 to 12 who could pet and handle him freely
Played nicely with the smaller dog in his last home, no scuffles
Knows Sit and Paw
Timid in the shelter but warms up fast, then stays glued to his person in the yard, tail wagging for pets
Big strong 72 pound boy with high energy who pulls, a harness helps
A5169156.story: His last home simply did not have time to train him. He is friendly, young, and desperate for someone who does.
A5169156.needs: A foster ready for a strong, high-energy dog who needs basic training. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5168978.name: LINUS
bullets: Six pounds of very frightened little dog
The family who found him says he was friendly with all their kids, even a 2 year old, and would sit and watch her play dolls
Found as a stray with a dog buddy, calm and quiet in a home
In the shelter he hides, trembles, and will snap if cornered or grabbed
Just this week he started approaching a soft-spoken handler, sniffing and wagging
A5168978.story: The shelter turned a gentle little house dog into a terrified one. A quiet living room would turn him back.
A5168978.needs: A calm, small-dog-savvy foster who will not force handling and will let him warm up on his own clock. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5078057.name: LOUIE
bullets: Compact 40 pound guy who thinks he is a lap dog, repeatedly climbed into volunteers' laps
Met three shelter dogs politely, happy to coexist, even threw a play bow
Loves the play pool, treat-chase games, and being brushed
Walks nicely on leash and ignores other dogs in passing
The kennel itself is what is breaking him, staff say he is falling apart inside it and lovely everywhere else
A5078057.story: Staff wrote it plainly: he does everything right outside the kennel, and the kennel is still going to cost him his life.
A5078057.needs: An experienced foster who can give him calm decompression time, best with older kids and slow dog intros.

A5168973.name: POPCORN
bullets: Greets people at the front of his kennel with perked ears and a wagging tail
Takes treats, leashes easily, walks with just a light pull
Independent explorer in the yard, very Chow, affection on his terms
Prefers pets on his back and body, not on top of his head
Hates going back into the kennel and fights it hard, and honestly, can you blame him
A5168973.story: He is two years old and telling everyone the same thing: get me out of this box. He needs someone who speaks Chow.
A5168973.needs: An experienced, Chow-savvy foster who lets him come to them. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A4455432.name: REX
bullets: A volunteer's exact words: "So gentle and sweet boy!" and "Love this little ole man"
Calm on a loose leash, ignores every dog he passes
Loves the play pool, back rubs, and sitting with his person
Great with the kids ages 10 to 14 in the home that found him
Fighting a cold he cannot kick in the shelter and skipping meals, no bite history
A4455432.story: Even sick and skipping meals, he still walks to the front of his kennel to ask for pets. That is who Rex is.
A4455432.needs: A quiet foster home to rest, finish his meds, and get vet follow-up for his lingering cold.

A5168957.name: STEFAN
bullets: Picked his own rescuer: darted into traffic, jumped into the finder's car, and refused to get out
His finder says friendly, calm, allowed all petting, just very vocal
Wagged his tail at other dogs passing through the lobby
Nervous and easily startled in the shelter, but takes treats gently and softens with a quiet voice
On meds for a mild cold, otherwise a healthy young boy
A5168957.story: He bet his whole life on a stranger's car door being open. Someone needs to prove him right.
A5168957.needs: A patient foster and decompression time in a quiet home. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5168969.name: SUSAN
bullets: 9 months old and 8 pounds
Came in with a dog friend, the two cuddle and clearly adore each other
Her finder says she was gentle with their 8 year old, just trembly and shy
Crate trained in the home, medium energy
Completely overwhelmed by the shelter, she trembles, hides, and cannot settle at all
A5168969.story: She is a baby drowning in noise and fear. In a quiet home with a calm dog to copy, she has every chance to bloom.
A5168969.needs: A quiet foster with decompression time, ideally with a mellow resident dog for confidence. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5168976.name: TONKA
bullets: 76 pound love bug with people: climbed on the bench between two handlers, rolled around for belly rubs, leaned into every pet
His finder says low energy homebody who loved relaxing in his crate
Crate trained, walks on leash with a light pull
Gets very worked up about other dogs right now and needs to be the only dog
On meds for a cold and a small healing scrape on his face
A5168976.story: With humans, Tonka is pure mush. He just needs a home where he does not have to share you.
A5168976.needs: An experienced only-dog foster, no dog parks, no dog intros for now. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5161330.name: BEAR
bullets: Greeted handlers with a loose, wiggly body and happy zoomies around the yard
Knows Sit, Stay, and Quiet, crate trained and house trained
Loves treats, just grabby, open palm please
Classic husky escape artist, needs secure fencing and a sturdy harness
His last home says an adult household with no other pets is the right fit, and he guards his food and toys
A5161330.story: Bear is a young husky who ended up with the wrong match, twice. With real husky people, he is a joyful, trainable goofball.
A5161330.needs: An experienced husky foster, adults only, no other pets, secure yard. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169069.name: FRITZ
bullets: 9 month old puppy found with his best friend, he literally rests his head on the other dog's back for comfort
His finder says skittish at first, then warmed up overnight with food and patience
Has never been leash trained, everything at the shelter terrifies him
Healthy, good appetite, vet gave him a clean check this week
A door dasher, so a foster home with secure doors matters
A5169069.story: He learned to trust a stranger in one single night. That is all he is asking for: one quiet night, and then another.
A5169069.needs: A quiet, patient foster with decompression time, ideally with a confident resident dog, treat him as a flight risk. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5168963.name: HANS
bullets: Wiggly and easy to leash, walks right out with his people
Loves being petted all over, comes back for more
Treat motivated and takes them gently, already knows "sit"
Other dogs are not his thing, he needs to be the one and only
No recorded bites
A5168963.story: Hans gives people his whole heart. He just wants a home where he never has to share it.
A5168963.needs: An experienced handler and an only-dog home with careful management around other dogs. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169060.name: HULK
bullets: Gentle on leash even when he is scared, walks softly beside you
Tolerates petting and never puts up a fight, just needs time to trust
So stressed in the shelter he has stopped eating
Quiet and slow, not a wild dog, a worried one
No recorded bites
A5169060.story: Hulk is not misbehaving, he is terrified. Every note in his file is a dog trying to disappear, and a quiet living room could bring him back.
A5169060.needs: A calm, patient foster and real decompression time. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169232.name: LIL BEAR
bullets: Lived 3 years in a home, surrendered only because his elderly owner couldn't keep up
Was playful with the family's little Chihuahua and gentle with their 3 year old
House trained, crate trained, leash trained
Loves to run when he's outside, hates baths, not a fan of fireworks
Shutting down at the shelter and refusing food
A5169232.story: Lil Bear had a person his whole life and lost her. He is not doing well in a kennel and he does not have to be.
A5169232.needs: A patient foster and a securely latched gate, he can be an escape artist. A vet should look at a minor eyelid issue on his left eye. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169068.name: LUCA
bullets: Young stray found with his sibling, the two stick together like glue
The person who found him said he was scared at first but warmed up overnight with food and patience
Never leash trained, he flattens and freezes, everything is new to him
Getting over a cough and already on his meds
A5169068.story: Luca is a scared teenager who proved once already that patience works on him. Someone just has to give him one more overnight.
A5169068.needs: A quiet, patient foster and decompression time, no pressure. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169059.name: MAC
bullets: 89 pounds of wiggly nub, whines for attention and leans in for pets
Takes treats gently and follows food anywhere
Chased a tennis ball, jumps up like a big puppy, still learning manners
Startles at touches he doesn't see coming, let him watch your hands
Finishing meds for kennel cough
A5169059.story: Mac wants to be near people so badly he stands with his paws on the bench begging for more. He just needs someone who moves slow and lets him say hello first.
A5169059.needs: An experienced handler who lets Mac initiate contact, no surprise grabs. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169249.name: MR SQUISH
bullets: Fetch machine, brings the ball back and lets you take it right from his mouth
Soft wiggly body, stays glued to his handler the whole yard visit
Startles at new things, then shakes it off and recovers fast
Had a fight with his kennel roommate, so he needs his own space for now
No recorded bites
A5169249.story: He is a 10 month old puppy who failed at sharing a tiny kennel, and it may cost him everything. In a yard with a person he is pure gold.
A5169249.needs: Only dog for now with very slow dog intros. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169161.name: PAC
bullets: 90 pound teenager, neutered, knows "sit" and is wildly food motivated
Plays fetch, chases toys with a bouncy gait and carries them back to you
Barks big at strangers at first, then melts fast with treats and warms right up
Previous home says good with the kids and lived with another large dog
Handlers could pet and handle him all over once he settled
A5169161.story: Pac is a giant baby behind a scary bark. Give him ten minutes and a treat pouch and he's yours.
A5169161.needs: An experienced big-dog handler, slow careful intros, and secure fencing, he has tried to climb one. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169251.name: PICKLES
bullets: Soft, gentle boy who leans his head into your hand for pets
Knows "sit" and takes treats like a gentleman
Stays right next to his person the entire yard visit
A little head shy, so slow easy hands win him over
Had a fight with his kennel roommate, needs his own space for now
A5169251.story: Pickles spent his whole evaluation pressed against his handler asking for love. Ten months old and already out of time.
A5169251.needs: Only dog for now with very slow dog intros, plus simple eye drops for mild irritation. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169132.name: PINK
bullets: Per her family: house trained, crate trained, dog-door pro
Knows sit, stay, and down, even responds to hand signals
Lived great with the other dog in her home and was playful with visiting kids
At the shelter she is scared and shut down, refusing food, but still licks hands and leans in for gentle pets
No recorded bites
A5169132.story: Pink lost her home through no fault of her own and the kennel is breaking her. Every eval says the same thing: she softens the moment someone is kind.
A5169132.needs: A quiet home and decompression time, she already knows how to be a good house dog. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169021.name: RUPERT
bullets: Small scruffy guy, about 33 pounds
Army crawls toward people with a fast wagging tail and licks hands
Eats tossed treats and softens with quiet voices
Terrified of leashes and being handled right now, and he will tell you when it's too much
No recorded bites
A5169021.story: Rupert wants to trust so badly that he crawls to you on his belly, tail going the whole time. Fear is the only thing standing between him and a couch.
A5169021.needs: An experienced, patient foster who lets him set the pace, hands-off decompression first. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169077.name: TEXAS
bullets: Total goofball, zoomies in the yard and fetch with every toy he can find
Knows "sit" and greets everyone with a soft wiggly body
Loves people, male and female handlers alike
Jumpy and mouthy when he's excited, big feelings and zero manners yet
Came in underweight and is on double meals to fill out
A5169077.story: Texas plays like a dog who never got to play before. He needs someone to teach him how to be as good as his heart already is.
A5169077.needs: An experienced foster who can channel big energy, ideally an adult home with training structure. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5168659.name: YOGURT
bullets: 15 pound senior gentleman, freshly neutered and cleaned up
Greets people with a soft body and wagging tail, licks hands
Takes treats gently and walks on his own four feet just fine
Does not want to be scooped up or grabbed, he'd rather walk himself, thank you
A5168659.story: Yogurt survived the streets at 8 years old and still wags at strangers. He just wants dignity: no grabbing, and a soft place to land.
A5168659.needs: A foster who respects his no-pick-up rule, plus vet follow-up for a heart murmur and rough teeth. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169192.name: PUFFLE
bullets: Tiny senior, just 5.6 pounds of black fluff
Sleeps deeply and wakes up slow, so he needs gentle, announced wake-ups
Grumbles about being picked up but settles once he's safe in your arms
Down to just a few teeth, so soft food only
Has a heart murmur and skin that needs some TLC
A5169192.story: Puffle is an old man who is scared, mostly toothless, and completely out of options. He doesn't need much, just softness at the end of a hard road.
A5169192.needs: Vet care for his heart, teeth, and skin through a medical rescue, and a quiet lap to recover on. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A4866197.name: NALA
bullets: Sweet spayed girl who knows "sit" and gives paw
Calm, loose-leash walker, easy in and out of the kennel every single time
Melts for butt scratches and takes treats gently
House trained and crate trained per her previous family
Wants to be your one and only dog
No recorded bites
A4866197.story: Nala has done everything right for a month. The only thing keeping her on this list is a stubborn cough that won't clear in a crowded shelter, and the cure is a quiet home.
A4866197.needs: An only-dog home with an experienced handler, meds and rest to finish beating her cough, and watchful doors, she will wander if one is left open.

A5168600.name: SPINACH
bullets: Gentle senior girl, calm and tolerant of handling
Walks beautifully on a loose leash and ignored other dogs on the way past
Knows "sit" and "lay"
Timid at first, then leans in and asks for pets
Lived peacefully with the finder's dogs, no cats please
No recorded bites
A5168600.story: Spinach was on the operating table for her spay when vets found lumps on her belly, and the surgery she needs is the one the shelter can't give her. She is sweet, steady, and worth saving.
A5168600.needs: Vet care through a rescue for removal of the lumps and follow-up testing, plus a soft place to heal. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169331.name: ARIEL
bullets: Seventy pound shepherd who came in as a stray after somebody stopped their car to help her
Let a handler take her out and walk her to the yard, and tolerated her leash being adjusted
Explored the whole yard on her own once she was outside
Ignores the other dogs completely on the way past their kennels
A5169331.story: She was coaxed into a stranger's car with food a week ago and has been in a concrete kennel ever since. She tucks, she watches, she will not take a treat from a hand. None of that is who she is, it is where she is.
A5169331.needs: A patient, experienced adult home with real decompression time and no pressure to interact. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5168981.name: CHARGER
bullets: Sits at the front of his kennel with a soft body and takes treats gently
Knows Sit
Wagged his tail and softened the moment the leash came out
Stays close to his handler in the yard with a loose tail wag
Walks past other dogs without reacting
A5168981.story: Charger is easy at the start and unravels as the minutes pass, panting, pacing the fence, crying. Five years old and sixty five pounds of a dog who wants a person and cannot cope with where he is.
A5168981.needs: An only-dog home with an experienced handler, and a rescue that can give him time to come down. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169149.name: CHOWDER
bullets: Lies calmly at the kennel door and is easy to leash
Walks past the other dogs without reacting to any of them
Came over to his handlers in the yard with a low, hopeful tail wag
Two years old and sixty five pounds
A5169149.story: He comes over, he asks, and then he loses his nerve and paces. At the gate he stands with his paws up, panting, wanting out. He is a young dog with no idea why he is here.
A5169149.needs: A quiet, experienced home with time and no rush to touch him. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169329.name: DOOGIE
bullets: An eight pound senior, already neutered
Settled once treats were tossed to him and started eating
Let a handler wrap him in a towel and carry him out without a fight
Explored the yard on his own, and eventually let himself be petted
A5169329.story: Nine years old, eight pounds, and trembling in a shelter. He starts every interaction growling because he is frightened, and finishes it letting a stranger stroke him. He has had his ears treated and his teeth looked at while he has been here.
A5169329.needs: A calm senior-friendly home, ideally somebody who has had a scared little dog before. Adults only. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169253.name: DUNKIN
bullets: Fifty two pounds, four years old
Walked into the transport crate on his own rather than being forced
Went out into the play yard by himself
Quiet throughout, no barking, no lunging
A5169253.story: Dunkin flattens his ears and licks his lips at the sight of a leash, and moves to the far side of any yard he is put in. He is not aggressive, he is trying very hard to be invisible. Cattle dogs are clever and this one has decided people are a problem to be avoided.
A5169253.needs: An experienced handler who understands shut-down dogs, an adults-only home, and weeks of leaving him alone to decide people are safe. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169147.name: JONAH
bullets: Approached his handler on his own with a neutral, calm body
Walked out to the yard and explored the whole thing, nose down
Came over when he was called and let himself be petted
Followed his handler around the yard by choice
Solicits attention from the staff who care for him
A5169147.story: Jonah is a two year old shepherd who will walk over to you and let you touch him, then flinch when your hand comes near his head. He is currently being treated for something contagious that a lot of shelter dogs pick up. He follows people because he wants to.
A5169147.needs: A patient home, gentle handling around his head, and a rescue that can finish his treatment. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5168816.name: KIKU
bullets: A hundred and four pounds of Akita, five years old
Takes treats out of the air and tolerates being petted in the yard
Softened and wagged his tail as soon as the leash appeared
Walks past other dogs and disengages from them on his own
Cleared his quarantine and is up to date on his shots
A5168816.story: Kiku is a serious dog who was probably somebody's whole world once. He is polite with people he trusts and clear about the ones he does not, and at his size that clarity has to be respected rather than argued with.
A5168816.needs: An experienced Akita or large-guardian home, adults only, no other dogs. He has reacted when startled, so his rescue and his foster need to be told everything and to move slowly. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169296.name: LADY
bullets: Forty two pounds, three years old
Comes forward for a treat when it is offered quietly and takes it
Silent in her kennel, no barking
Grabs the leash and lets it go rather than doing anything with it
A5169296.story: Lady says no clearly. She warns, she postures, and she has never followed through on any of it. That is a frightened dog with good manners about her own fear, and it reads as dangerous on a kennel card when it is actually restraint.
A5169296.needs: An experienced adults-only home, no children, no other pets to start, and a rescue with a behavior person. This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169389.name: MUPPET
bullets: Six pounds, six years old, already spayed
Let a handler pick her up and carry her, and stayed in her arms
Allowed light petting on her head once she was out of the kennel
Stayed beside her handler on the floor for a while before retreating
A5169389.story: A six pound dog cannot fight a shelter, so she growls and trembles and hides at the back instead. She has stopped eating. She is somebody's small old dog and she is not coping with any of this.
A5169389.needs: A very quiet adults-only home, someone experienced with frightened small dogs, and a rescue that can get her eating again. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169242.name: OLIVE
bullets: Sixty seven pounds, six years old, already spayed
Came out of her kennel calmly and walked out to the yard
Explored the yard happily on her own
Came running the moment somebody said the word treat
Passed her pre-operative exam with everything normal
A5169242.story: Olive guards what is hers. She had her dinner and a good chew at the front of her kennel and she told a stranger to leave them alone, which is a completely reasonable thing for a dog to think. Away from her food she is a middle-aged collie mix who comes when you say treat.
A5169242.needs: An adults-only home that will feed her somewhere private and leave her alone while she eats. She does not need a rescue, so if this is your kind of dog you can go and get her.

A5169274.name: PEPPERCORN
bullets: Eighty three pounds, two years old
Lying calmly in the middle of her kennel when staff came
Came forward when treats were offered
Moved closer to her handler while a photo was being taken, and let herself be petted on the head
A5169274.story: She would not walk out of her kennel and had to be carried, and once she was outside she chose to come closer to the person with her. She has a cold and a small eye problem, both common and both fixable. Two years old and enormous and frightened.
A5169274.needs: An experienced large-breed home with quiet handling, plus a rescue that can treat her eye and her cold. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5168821.name: STARBURST
bullets: A six month old puppy, thirty pounds
Let a handler pick her up and stayed calm the whole way
Allowed petting all over once she settled on the floor
Ate hot dogs out of a stranger's hand
Came back to sit next to her handler when a noise startled her
A5168821.story: She came in with heat stroke in July and survived it. Six months old, hiding in a corner, and still choosing to move closer to the person sitting on the floor with her. A handler put soft music on for her. That is what she needs, and more time than a shelter can give.
A5168821.needs: A quiet home willing to raise a shy puppy properly, with patience and no crowds. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169264.name: WINSTON
bullets: Twenty five pounds, three years old
Rode calmly in the crate to the meeting room
Quiet throughout, no barking or growling
A5169264.story: Winston hides in the corner and thrashes when hands come near him, and then travels calmly once he is somewhere enclosed and quiet. Everything he does says he has learned that being grabbed is what happens to him. Three years old and small enough to disappear in a shelter.
A5169264.needs: An experienced adults-only home that will let him come out on his own terms, and no handling he has not agreed to. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169591.name: NAME UNKNOWN
bullets: Eighteen pounds, four years old
At the front of her kennel with a soft wiggly body and a wagging tail
Let a handler pet her everywhere
Stood politely for her vaccinations and was carried back to her kennel
Rated green by the shelter on her behavior
A5169591.story: Nobody has given her a name yet. She is a four year old French Bulldog who wags at everybody and lets a stranger do anything, and she is on this list for a skin condition that is already being treated. She is the easiest dog on this page.
A5169591.needs: Somebody to finish her skin treatment and give her a name. Must go through a New Hope partner rescue.

A5169084.name: Forky
bullets: Knows sit, takes treats gently, carries toys around and chews them
Jumps repeatedly on people, mouths at hands when reached for from the front, grabs and pulls at clothing and leash when aroused
Becomes tense and pulls hard toward other dogs passing—watched one through a fence with forward posture, whining and brief growling
Returned to the shelter after five days because the adopter said he was too young and hard to control
35 pounds, a year old, high energy, pulls hard on leash, not housetrained
A5169084.story: Forky is a young pit bull type with puppy energy still running the show. He knows a sit command and settles with toys, but when he gets worked up he jumps, mouths, and grabs at whatever's in reach—leash, clothing, treat pouch. He's been in the shelter less than two weeks and the stress is sharpening his edges.
A5169084.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Forky needs an experienced handler who understands arousal and impulse control in young, strong dogs, who won't be rattled by mouthing or jumping, and who has no other dogs in the home. He is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue with behavior support by end of business August 16th.

A5167231.name: Fresa
bullets: Puts her front paws on your lap and leans in hard for petting, licks hands and face gently, follows handlers around the yard
Knows sit, takes treats nicely, walks on a loose leash
Soft and affiliative with people once outside her kennel—wagging tail, relaxed mouth, calm body
Showed escalating arousal and fence fighting behavior during a dog greeting test, hackles raised, biting at fence, harder to redirect
Shut down hard in the kennel—self-injuring from stress, resisting return, though staff note she has shown some improvement since early July
A5167231.story: Fresa is a two-year-old pit mix who becomes a different dog once she's out of her kennel. With people, she's gentle and affectionate, leaning into touch, offering calm attention. But the shelter environment is breaking her down—the constant noise, the other dogs, the lack of control over anything. She needs out now, before the clock runs out.
A5167231.needs: This is not a beginner's dog. Fresa needs an experienced handler who understands fear and stress, can give her time to decompress in a quiet home, and has the skill to work through leash reactivity and dog selectivity. No dog parks, no multi-dog household until a professional says otherwise. She has five days.

A5167656.name: Nori
bullets: Sits, stays, lays down on cue and carries a stuffed toy around the yard like it's her most important possession
Leans in for affection, sprawls out in the sun with her stuffy on her lap, comes back to check in with people she trusts
Pulls hard on a flat collar but walks well in a front-clip harness
Needs to be the only dog—returned after one day when an immediate introduction to another dog didn't go well
Medical priority due to nosebleeds causing acute anemia
A5167656.story: Nori is a three-year-old pittie mix who loves people, knows her basics, and has the kind of high energy that comes with a wagging tail and a favorite toy. She's been in and out of the shelter system and needs a home that understands she doesn't do well with other dogs. Right now she's fighting something harder—nosebleeds that have left her anemic and on a countdown.
A5167656.needs: Only dog household, no exceptions. Someone who can manage a strong puller on leash and match her energy level. This is a medical priority case and she must be pulled by a New Hope Partner rescue by end of business August 16th.

A5169183.name: Orchid
bullets: Stays close to people in the yard, leans in for pets, then moves away to pace
Approached handlers for contact but struggled when asked to keep four paws on the floor
Startles when surprised—body low, ears back, heavy panting
A5169183.story: Orchid is a young shepherd living in a state of high alert. She seeks comfort from people but doesn't yet know how to settle into it. The world feels unpredictable to her right now, and she's working hard to manage that fear.
A5169183.needs: Orchid needs an experienced handler who understands fearful dogs and won't rush her, a home with no small children, and a plan for helping her learn the world is safer than she believes. This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. She is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a qualified partner rescue by end of business August 16.

A5143991.name: Rocky
bullets: Two years old, lived with his family since puppyhood—housetrained, crate trained, knows sit, paw, come, and his name
Surrendered because a new apartment won't allow his breed, then bit during intake handling and went into quarantine

Handlers report he shifts hard between shut-down fear and explosive over-arousal—freezing at the back of his kennel baring teeth, then lunging at the door, then softening in the yard when given space and time
In the yard he explored, marked, jumped up for attention, leaned into handlers for petting, took treats—but needed distance and predictability to settle
Barks at other dogs on leash, pulls hard toward them in the building
A5143991.story: Rocky spent his whole life in one home until an apartment wouldn't take him. The shelter terrifies him and he shows it—big, loud, all teeth and thrashing—but in the yard with patient handlers he softened, leaned in, asked to be touched. He is not a simple dog and this is not a simple fear.
A5143991.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Rocky needs an experienced handler who understands fearful reactivity, can read a dog coming unglued, and won't take it personally. No kids. Must be pulled by a New Hope partner rescue by close of business August 16.

A5169289.name: Wednesday
bullets: Retreats to the back of her kennel when people approach, watches with darting eyes, body frozen
Flinches and pulls away when handlers move quickly or reach toward her
Took treats gently from open hands in the yard but wouldn't approach people on her own
A5169289.story: Wednesday is a young mastiff mix shutting down hard under shelter pressure. She moves through the day tense and hypervigilant, startling at gestures, unsure what comes next. Underneath the fear is a dog who took treats softly and tolerated leash handling without snapping, but she is not holding together here.
A5169289.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Wednesday needs an experienced foster with a quiet home, no sudden movements, and the patience to let a frightened dog decompress at her own pace. She is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a registered rescue partner by end of day August 16.

A5169745.name: Los
bullets: Handlers describe soft body language, wagging tail, coming forward to ask for attention at the front of his kennel
Walked on leash and allowed all handling, scanning, and vaccinations with muzzle restraint as standard protocol
Placed green for behavior based on kennel presence and intake notes
A5169745.story: Los is a two-year-old gray and white pittie who showed up friendly and willing at intake, soliciting attention from handlers even while dealing with a treatable skin condition. He has six days to find a rescue partner willing to see past ringworm and into the soft-bodied dog underneath.
A5169745.needs: Needs a foster home experienced with medical foster dogs and comfortable with ringworm treatment protocols. Los is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a qualified partner rescue no later than 5:30 a.m. on August 18th.

A5169191.name: Marlin
bullets: A seven-year-old cream terrier, eight pounds, trembling in the back of his kennel when handlers approach.
Came forward to put his paws on a handler's leg, shaking and whining, but flinched hard when touched.
Has not been eating his kibble and needs dental work the shelter cannot provide.
A5169191.story: Marlin is so frightened he can barely let people help him, even though some part of him wants to try. He recoils from touch, defecates from stress, hides under blankets. His mouth hurts and he has six days.
A5169191.needs: This is not a beginner's dog. Marlin needs someone who has worked with deeply fearful dogs, who will not rush him, and who can get him the dental care that will save his life. He is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue.

A5168104.name: Nebula
bullets: Walked easily on leash through the shelter, calm and nonreactive when passing other dogs in kennels
Soft and gentle through handling, sat for treats, gave kisses when petted
Loved playing with water from the hose during yard time
Approached handlers slowly at first but warmed with soft voice and patience
Took treats nicely, allowed petting all over
A5168104.story: Nebula came in with another dog in July and spent her first days quiet and watchful. By the second week she was standing at the kennel door waiting for company, leaning into pets, playing in the water. Now she's facing a medical deadline for a respiratory illness that won't resolve in a shelter environment.
A5168104.needs: A home that understands decompression—she takes time to settle but blooms once she does. Nebula is listed urgent medical and has six days left. Proper dog introductions only after she's had time to decompress.

A5168105.name: Pound Cake
bullets: Seeks out attention from handlers and leans in for petting, allows handling all over including while being toweled off in the heat.
Knows sit, takes treats gently, plays with toys but releases on command.
Calm energy in the yard, stayed near the fan on hot days, plays in water and pools.
Ignores kenneled dogs when walking past, somewhat pulls on leash but redirects when needed.
Has been at the shelter over a month with persistent respiratory illness that is not improving.
A5168105.story: Pound Cake came in as a stray with another dog in mid-July, a mellow two-year-old who knows some basics and just wants to be near his person. He's been battling a respiratory infection the whole time he's been kenneled, and it's wearing him down.
A5168105.needs: A foster who can get him out of the shelter environment so he can finally recover, with space to decompress and a plan for slow introductions to any other animals in the home. He's on the medical priority list with six days left.

A5168507.name: Bear
bullets: Came in with a bonded kennel mate after his person passed away, lived four years in a single-adult home where he was the calm, relaxed dog in the household
In shelter, startles when handlers approach too fast or corner him—has growled once when boxed in, but out in the yard stands soft and presses in for petting, walks easily on leash
Described by the person who knew him as friendly with strangers, house-trained, leash-trained though he pulls, and calm around other dogs, rabbits, and birds
A5168507.story: Bear lost his person. His person's brother drove him to Arizona and surrendered him because there was nowhere else for an 80-pound shepherd mix to go. The world got small and frightening fast, and Bear is struggling with handlers in the kennel but softening in open space when given time.
A5168507.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Bear needs someone who understands a dog shaped by grief and fear, who will not corner him or rush him, and who has the skill to work with a dog who growls when he feels trapped. Because he appears bonded to his kennel mate, a home able to take both would mean everything. Bear is New Hope Only with five days left—a qualified rescue partner must pull him by close of business August 16th.

A5168508.name: Luna
bullets: Came in with another dog after her owner passed away, and shelter staff say the two appear bonded through the evaluation process
Shuts down hard when separated from her companion, trembling and pancaking in the back of the kennel, whale-eyed and unable to move toward handlers
With her companion nearby, warms slowly to people, eventually leaning in for petting, climbing into a kiddie pool, and following handlers around the yard
Walks on leash with pulling, allows handling for leash removal, enters kennel willingly when her companion is with her
A5168508.story: Luna is seven and her person died. The brother who drove her here from out of state said she lived inside and out, was friendly, calm. What the shelter sees is a dog whose world collapsed, who cannot function alone, who only breathes right when the other dog from her old life is close.
A5168508.needs: Must be pulled by a partner rescue no later than close of business August 16. Cannot be separated from A5168507. Needs a foster who understands terrified dogs and will not rush her, and who has space and patience for a bonded pair.

A5168053.name: Lynx
bullets: Runs hard zoomies in the play yard, mouth open and tail wagging, then leans against his handler for petting
Walks on leash with moderate pull, doesn't react to neighboring dogs, returns when called
Shuts down hard in his kennel—tense body, tucked tail, shows teeth when stressed by confinement—but softens completely once out
A5168053.story: Lynx is a five-year-old husky mix who loves people and does beautifully outside his kennel, but the shelter is breaking him. He's running out of time because the kennel stress is escalating and he has three days left.
A5168053.needs: Experienced handler who understands a dog under this much pressure and won't take the kennel behavior personally. Older kids only, slow introductions, no other dogs until he's had two weeks to decompress. Deadline is August 16.

A5169543.name: Bow
bullets: Came in at 9 months with her littermates when the family moved to a small apartment and couldn't keep three large young dogs
Before shelter, her people said she was energetic and affectionate, learning fetch, working on house training and not pulling on leash, knew sit and stay with a treat
First days in shelter she shut down hard—wouldn't take treats, darted away from handlers, paced and couldn't settle, showed whale eye and froze when reached for
By day four handlers noted soft body and low tail wag at kennel front, solicited attention and licked hands through the door
At 50 pounds and still learning basics, she's a big young dog who came apart under shelter stress
A5169543.story: Bow is a 9-month-old who lived her whole short life with her littermates until the move that brought all three here. The shelter terrified her at first and she showed it the way a young dog with no other options does—by running, by freezing, by trying to disappear. By the second half of the week she was seeking contact again, but the damage was done.
A5169543.needs: Bow is marked New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue by close of business August 17th. She needs a foster with dog experience who understands that fear in a 50-pound adolescent is a serious thing, that she will need time and space and no pressure while she learns the world won't hurt her. This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise.

A5169536.name: Elsa
bullets: Lived with her bonded companion, another German Shepherd, for two years in a home with four kids
Handled being around cats without incident
In shelter evaluation: kept her distance, paced, took treats but stayed wary, barked when uncertain, moved in low postures with tension through her whole body
A5169536.story: Elsa came in with the dog she's lived alongside since she was a puppy. Her family said she'd growl at unfamiliar people but had never bitten. Here, she shows a dog whose fear runs deep—tense, watchful, struggling to trust even when someone sits quietly and waits.
A5169536.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Elsa needs someone who understands fearful shepherds, has no young children, and can give her the time and space to decide people might be safe. She is New Hope Only with four days left, which means a partner rescue must pull her by close of business August 17th.

A5161444.name: Francis
bullets: Strong 72-pound shepherd who pulls hard on leash and rushes kennel doors with high energy—handlers describe him as green in the yard, soliciting attention, leaning in for pets, running after squeak toys
Lives with another large German Shepherd at his last home, which lasted just over a month before the owner said he was too strong to manage
Kennel stress is climbing—bites at leashes and latches when aroused, pushes out of doors, requires two handlers and specific management to move safely
A5161444.story: Francis came back to MCACC a month after adoption because his strength overwhelmed his person. He's a big shepherd with big energy who softens in the yard, but weeks in a kennel have turned his arousal into something harder to manage. He needs out now, and he needs someone who knows what they're doing.
A5161444.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Francis needs an experienced handler who can manage a strong, high-energy shepherd with escalating kennel stress and a German Shepherd-savvy rescue partner who can pull him by close of business August 17th. New Hope Only—he must be pulled by a registered rescue partner.

A5169597.name: Fred
bullets: Knows sit and stay, catches treats mid-air, takes them gently from your hand
Pulls hard on leash, door-dashes when he sees an opening, chases cats outside
Jumps onto people when excited, mouths at hands when redirected, climbs into laps on benches
Ramps up fast in the play yard—soft and friendly at first, then pacing, whining, wide eyes, won't settle
Lived inside for a year with another dog he mostly ignored, crate trained, housetrained
A5169597.story: Fred is a 67-pound shepherd with a year of indoor life behind him and a motor that runs hot. His previous owner surrendered him because of a change in living situation. In the shelter he starts every interaction soft and wiggly, then escalates into jumping, mouthing, and intense face-licking that he cannot dial back down, even with redirection.
A5169597.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Fred needs an experienced handler who understands high arousal and can manage a strong dog who does not self-regulate when excited. He must be pulled by a New Hope partner rescue no later than August 17.

A4666391.name: Oso
bullets: Lived with two large dogs and played well with them, though he guarded his sleeping spot on the bed at night
Walked right next to handlers, knew sit and shake, took treats gently, leaned in for affection
Bit his owner when reached for—sensitive to touch on his head and hindquarters, snapped when moved or touched in ways he didn't like
Sought closeness and followed his person around, wanted to sleep with them
Stopped eating in the shelter for days at a stretch both times he's been there
A4666391.story: Oso is a 90-pound dog who wants to be close to his person and knows how to be gentle when he feels safe. But he's also a dog who will bite when touched wrong, and his last owner had him only three and a half months before that happened. He's back at the shelter now with a bite on record and four days left.
A4666391.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Oso needs an experienced handler who understands pressure, boundaries, and resource guarding, and who won't reach for him carelessly. He must be pulled by a New Hope Partner rescue no later than close of business August 17th.

A5169496.name: Tristan
bullets: Stayed near handler in yard, sat behind chair or stood beside, allowed petting all over
Stopped to sniff another dog through fence, gentle tail wag, interested
Explored yard with nose to ground, approached handler and leaned in for pets
Startles easily, shuts down hard at kennel gate—pancakes, thrashes, spins
Refused all treats across multiple days, hid in back of kennel, would not eat
A5169496.story: Tristan is a young Great Dane mix who wants to trust people but is drowning in fear at the shelter. In the yard he softens, stays close, leans in. At the kennel door he unravels—thrashing, spinning, throwing himself to the ground rather than go back in.
A5169496.needs: This is not a beginner's dog. Tristan needs a rescue partner experienced with fear-based behavior who can meet him where he is and give him time to decompress in a home. He must be pulled by a New Hope Partner by close of business August 17.

A5169164.name: Walter
bullets: Came in with another dog after being found as a stray.
Shuts down hard in the shelter—freezes, backs into corners, won't take treats, whale-eyed and terrified when handlers reach for him.
Once outside, softened slightly with one handler, allowed light petting, explored the yard with his tail tucked.
Has a bite on record from intake—came up behind someone who was trying to pick up a loose dog and bit their leg.
A5169164.story: Walter is a two-year-old pit mix drowning in fear. The shelter terrifies him so deeply he can barely function, but in the yard he showed flickers of who he might be with time and patience. He has a bite history and this is not a simple case.
A5169164.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Walter needs an experienced handler who understands fear-based behavior, can give him structure and space to decompress, and knows that progress will be slow. No small dogs, no chaotic environments. Must be pulled by a New Hope Partner rescue by August 17th.

A5169489.name: Dani
bullets: Five-month-old puppy who approached handlers with a soft, wiggly body and solicited attention through an entire meet and greet
Takes treats nicely and allowed all handling, picking up, and carrying without resistance
Has a fractured left hind leg and is not putting weight on it, but stayed friendly and gentle throughout evaluations
A5169489.story: Dani came in as a typical puppy—playful, friendly, jumping at kennel doors to say hello—and then staff noticed she wasn't using her back leg. She has a tibial fracture that needs treatment, but her spirit hasn't dimmed. She's still the same soft, wiggly girl who wants your attention and takes every interaction in stride.
A5169489.needs: Dani needs a foster through a New Hope partner rescue who can manage her medical care and give her a quiet place to heal. She has five days left and is flagged as medical priority. If no rescue pulls her by end of business August 18th, her time is up.

A5167948.name: Esmie
bullets: Found as a stray with another dog, soft and wiggly with handlers, takes treats gently and leans in for petting
Walks on leash with light to moderate pull, checks in with handler, explored yard calmly
Reacted when other dogs walked past kennel, redirected twice onto kennel mate, separated after scuffles
Has persistent respiratory illness requiring medical attention
A5167948.story: Esmie came in as a stray with another dog and has been gentle and affectionate with every person who's worked with her. But watching other dogs walk by triggered reactions she couldn't manage, and twice she turned that frustration on her kennel mate. She's been on the medical priority list for ongoing respiratory disease.
A5167948.needs: Only dog home. Someone who understands that reactivity to passing dogs is manageable with structure, but requires commitment and is not a beginner situation. Proper decompression time before any dog introductions are even considered. Medical foster prepared to continue treatment for respiratory illness.

A5166121.name: Apricot
bullets: Stayed calm with the person who found her wandering, rode in a car, took treats
Pulls hard on leash, paces and jumps in the kennel, high energy that hasn't settled in shelter
Lunged at a small dog during intake; in recent evaluations pulled hard toward other dogs, barked, went tense
A5166121.story: Apricot was found wandering near a street and lured into a car with treats by a stranger, so someone gentle is in there. But seventy-two pounds of unsettled energy in a concrete kennel for two months has her climbing the walls. She's mouthy when aroused, jumps at faces, and her reactions to other dogs have gotten sharper as the days pile up.
A5166121.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Apricot needs an experienced handler who understands high-arousal behavior and can give her the structure and space to decompress outside of shelter chaos. New Hope Only, so she must be pulled by a partner rescue by close of business August 18th.

A5169619.name: Doris
bullets: Found as a stray with three other dogs, walked on leash, lived around kids and other dogs before intake.
Shuts down hard when afraid—freezes in place, stays tucked in a corner or a bucket, moves in slow motion with her body low.
After sitting quietly for several minutes in the yard, she walked over to her handler, sniffed, and allowed chin scratches before moving away again.
A5169619.story: Doris is a young husky who goes still and small when the world feels too big. She doesn't know commands and she doesn't trust easily, but when given time and space in the yard, she eventually came to her handler on her own terms. That moment matters—it's the shape of who she could become with patience.
A5169619.needs: Doris needs a quiet foster home with husky experience, no young kids, and someone who understands that fear this deep takes months, not weeks, to unwind. This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. She is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue no later than 5:30am on August 19th.

A5169588.name: Goalie
bullets: Found as a stray with skin trouble, bleeding from scratching; finder said he sat on command, walked on leash, let them touch his food bowl, bathed without protest.
In the shelter kennel, he alarm-barks and bites at the leash when handlers approach, sometimes low-growls, sometimes shuts down and won't eat.
On good days, once leashed and outside, he's played, zoomed, leaned into a handler for petting, taken treats gently.
A5169588.story: Goalie is a 3-year-old pit bull who arrived itchy and raw and has since unraveled in the stress of the kennel. Whoever gets him out will meet a different dog than the one the shelter sees—but getting him there will take patience, skill, and a long enough timeline to let him rebuild trust.
A5169588.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. He needs an experienced foster who understands fear and knows how to wait it out, in a calm adult home with no other animals. New Hope Only—he must be pulled by a partner rescue by end of day August 18.

A5169524.name: Mcdouble
bullets: Takes hot dogs gently from an open hand when calm
Watched treat bag with interest, ears forward
Growls, lunges, and snaps at leash and gate when handlers approach to move him or take him out
A5169524.story: Mcdouble is a 19-pound French Bulldog who is terrified of being handled or moved from his kennel. When distracted with food, he softens. When people reach for him or present a leash, he escalates fast—growling, lunging, biting at the leash, air-snapping near gloved hands.
A5169524.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Mcdouble needs an experienced handler who understands fear aggression, can work slowly, and won't push him past threshold. He must be pulled by a New Hope Partner rescue no later than August 18.

A5164525.name: Minnie
bullets: Seeks out affection, loves to splash and roll in pools, jumps up when excited and wants to sit in laps
Walks on leash with some pulling, knows sit, plays fetch, high energy
Mixed signals around other dogs: sometimes wagging and playful, sometimes barking and fence-fighting, arousal escalates when confined
Reported good with a toddler during brief stray hold, easy for handlers to work with outside the kennel
Showing significant kennel stress after three months inside
A5164525.story: Minnie came in as a stray in May and has been waiting since. Outside her kennel she's a love bug who splashes in pools and climbs into laps, but the confinement is breaking her down. She's inconsistent around other dogs and her arousal builds fast when she can't get space, so she'll need someone who understands what that means and how to manage it.
A5164525.needs: Home with older kids only, no other dogs without very careful assessment by someone experienced with dog reactivity, and the time to let her decompress after months of this. This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. She has four days left.

A5169538.name: Nougat
bullets: Shuts down hard in the shelter—won't eat, won't take treats, moves with his tail tucked and his mouth open panting.
Freezes when approached, then whale-eyes and licks his lips while handlers try to coax him along.
Panic escalates fast under pressure—thrashes, bites at the leash, tries to jump out of a carrier rather than be confined.
A5169538.story: Nougat is a two-year-old cattle dog mix drowning in fear. He came in terrified and the shelter environment has only made it worse. He needs someone who understands that a dog this shut down isn't being stubborn—he's overwhelmed—and that the dog he could be won't show up until he feels safe.
A5169538.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Nougat needs an experienced foster with a quiet home, no expectations, and the patience to let a frightened dog decompress at his own pace. New Hope Only—he must be pulled by a partner rescue by August 18th.

A4348225.name: Polar Pop
bullets: Handlers report she sits on command, takes treats gently, walks easily on leash, and solicits affection—one described her jumping onto a bench to kiss their face.
Good with the household dog and shares toys, space, and treats without guarding; described as great with teenagers in the home and kids of all ages in the neighborhood.
Surrendered after severely injuring a cat—the owner reported she became fixated, grabbed the cat by the head, and shook it violently, requiring surgery.
A4348225.story: Polar Pop is an eight-year-old husky who's affectionate with people and shares her space graciously with dogs. But she has a documented history with small animals that cannot be managed away, and the outcome for the cat in her last home was catastrophic.
A4348225.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. She needs an experienced handler in a home with no cats, no small animals, and solid containment—someone who understands prey drive at this level and can keep everyone safe. She is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue with the resources to evaluate and place her appropriately.

A4656315.name: Roxy
bullets: Lived ten years with the same family—friendly with adults and kids, knew sit and stay, door-trained and crate-trained
Approached handlers softly, rolled over for belly rubs, accepted treats from unfamiliar people after warming up
Guarded her kennel mate hard—flagged tail, raised hackles, air-snapped and bit at a handler's gloved hand when they tried to interact with the other dog
A4656315.story: Roxy came in with two other dogs when her family moved out of state. In her home she was the cuddly lapdog who chased birds in the yard. In the shelter she is tense and terrified, and when handlers tried to approach her kennel mate, she escalated fast—groaning, jumping, biting the glove. That is fear and resource guarding under pressure, not who she was for a decade.
A4656315.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Roxy needs an experienced handler who understands fear-based guarding, a home without other dogs, and space to decompress far from the chaos that broke her open. She is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue by close of business August 18th.

A5168427.name: Danny Devito
bullets: Found as a stray and has been frozen with fear in the shelter—barely takes a step or two on leash before stopping, sometimes so shut down he had to be carried in a taxi cart to reach the play yard.
Once he feels safe, he climbs into laps, leans in hard for pets, gives kisses, and ignores other dogs walking past.
Sick with kennel cough and running out of time—listed as medical priority with six days left.
A5168427.story: Danny Devito came in terrified and he has stayed terrified, the kind of scared that roots a dog to the ground. In quiet moments with patient handlers he softens completely, all weight and warmth and gentle need. He has been sick for weeks and the shelter cannot wait much longer.
A5168427.needs: A foster who understands fear shutdown, who will go slow and not ask for courage he does not have yet. Someone home often, no young kids. He needs out now—medically and emotionally, this is urgent.

A5165552.name: Andy
bullets: Walked calmly on leash through the shelter, ignored other dogs in kennels, took treats gently from volunteers' hands
Rolled over for belly rubs in the play yard, leaned into handlers for petting, came when called with a relaxed body
Stood in the water tub and sipped from it during outdoor time
Kenneled life is breaking him—handlers report lowered head, flattened ears, and shut-down body language when confined, though he transforms outside the kennel
Came in with two other dogs in May, has lived with multiple dogs and puppies before
A5165552.story: Andy is a young shepherd mix who knows how to be soft with people—gentle with treats, easy on leash, the kind of dog who puts his front paws in your lap and leans in. But the kennel is erasing him. He shreds blankets, startles easily, and shrinks into himself behind bars, though the same dog who flattens his ears at leash-up will roll over for you in the yard a minute later. He has four days left.
A5165552.needs: Older children only, 12 and up. Andy needs an experienced home that understands what decompression actually requires—time, space, patience, and no pressure. He will need secure fencing (he's been flagged for escape risk) and a slow approach to any dog introductions until he's settled. Placement needed by close of business August 19th.

A5169756.name: Charles Barkley
bullets: Shuts down in the kennel—trembling, frozen against the back wall, avoiding eye contact
Accepts treats gently from a handler's hand once he starts to trust, and will slowly move closer
Pulls away when touched, whips his head around when startled, needs space and patience to feel safe
A5169756.story: Charles Barkley is terrified. He arrived at the shelter in a net, and the fear has not lifted. He trembles, he retreats, he watches from the corner. But underneath that terror is a dog who will inch forward for treats, who will sit beside you if you don't rush him, who takes food gently even when his whole body is still shaking.
A5169756.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. He needs an experienced, patient foster who understands deep fear and will not force interaction—someone who can let him decompress for as long as it takes. Charles Barkley is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue by August 19.

A5168502.name: Coby
bullets: Plays fetch, trades toys easily, knows sit, solicits attention by leaning against you with soft body
Has lived with three young children (2, 5, and 7) and been friendly and playful with them
Came back after two weeks because his energy level was more than the home could handle
Strong puller on leash, was walked with a gentle leader
Does well in a crate when covered with a blanket
A5168502.story: Coby is an 83-pound shepherd who came back through no fault of his own. He was more dog than his adopters expected. He is young, strong, and needs a handler who can work with high arousal and redirect a big, intense dog before that energy tips over into frustration. In the shelter environment, that tipping point is getting closer.
A5168502.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Coby needs an experienced shepherd home that understands overstimulation and can give him structure, exercise, and calm leadership. He must be pulled by a New Hope Partner rescue by end of day August 19.

A5169779.name: Coin
bullets: Found running in traffic, jumping fences. The finder sat with her for thirty minutes before she let him touch her and get her to safety.
Lived with a small dog and a cat, allowed all sniffing and play. Appeared leash trained, though sometimes freezes.
Explored the yard quietly, tail down, keeping distance. Alarm barked when approached in the kennel. Side-eyed handlers when startled, then took treats from the grass.
Once trust starts, she pancakes and allows careful petting. Skin crawled when touched on the back. Easily startled by noise and movement.
Low growled when handlers reached for her leash, then accepted it. Walked slowly back to her kennel, tense but cooperative.
A5169779.story: Coin is a two-year-old dog whose fear runs so deep she shuts down when cornered and growls when startled by a hand coming toward her. The finder who pulled her from traffic said she was sweet once she built trust, and the shelter has seen that too, but it takes time she does not have here. This is a dog who needs someone who understands that fear and handling sensitivity are not the same as aggression, and who will not rush her.
A5169779.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Coin needs an experienced, patient foster who can give her the months it will take to decompress and learn that hands mean safety. She must be pulled by a rescue partner no later than close of business August 19.

A5166664.name: Erin
bullets: Showed up as a stray, skittish at first then friendly enough to jump into the finder's car after 11 days
Fence fights other dogs in the shelter with intense focus—lunging, curling lips, growling, hard to redirect even with leash pressure
When calm, leans into people for petting, knows sit, explores with a soft body, takes treats gently
A5166664.story: Erin walked into someone's life as a stray and tried to fit in—slept beside them, wanted to play with their dogs, chased their cats like prey. The shelter has made her reactivity toward other dogs much worse. She still softens for people who give her time, but the clock and thekennel stress are working against her.
A5166664.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Erin needs an experienced handler who understands dog reactivity, can manage it safely, and has no other dogs or cats. She is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue with the resources to support her behavior long-term.

A5169577.name: Loofy
bullets: Found wandering a parking lot, warmed up after being offered water, lived with the finder for 11 hours—friendly with their older large dog, knew 'paw,' took treats, walked on leash
In the shelter yard he explored independently at first, then leaned close to handlers, prompted petting but stayed alert, scanning his surroundings the whole time
Didn't eat for the first day or two but has been stretching, soliciting attention, and coming to his kennel door since then
A5169577.story: Loofy is a 102-pound young shepherd mix who showed up out of nowhere and acted like he'd known people before. He's friendly but watchful, the kind of dog whose wheels are always turning.
A5169577.needs: This is not a beginner's dog. He needs experienced hands who understand a dog still figuring out whether the world is safe. New Hope Only—Loofy must be pulled by a partner rescue no later than 5:30 a.m. on August 20th.

A5169690.name: Sigrun
bullets: Bonded strongly with her last handler in two months, friendly and allowed all handling with that one person
In the shelter, shuts down hard—wide-eyed stare, alarm barking, dodging the leash, won't take treats, pushing at fences, won't approach handlers
Guarded the home she knew: barked and air-snapped when anyone but her person came through the door
Anxious around other dogs—whines at small dogs on walks, tries to run from large ones
Lost her original owner to death, was rehomed once, then surrendered when the guarding became unmanageable
A5169690.story: Sigrun is a seven-year-old shepherd who has been through too much loss in too short a time. She attached deeply to the woman who took her in after her owner died, but two months was not enough to feel safe when strangers entered that home. Now the shelter has broken whatever confidence she had left.
A5169690.needs: This is not a beginner's dog and we will not pretend otherwise. Sigrun needs an experienced handler who understands fear-based territoriality, lives alone or with no foot traffic, and has the time to rebuild trust from the ground up. No children. She is New Hope Only and must be pulled by a partner rescue no later than close of business August 19th.

A5169672.name: Tabasco
bullets: Six-pound brown and white Chihuahua, two years old, found as a stray and brought in scared.
Finder said he got along well with her and played with the children in her home, but did not like other people.
In the shelter he is deeply frightened—paces, won't settle, freezes at doorways, and defends himself when handlers reach toward him.
When given space and time he sat near a handler in the yard and allowed brief petting along his side.
Takes treats when not overwhelmed but shuts down hard under pressure.
